entries.title: Penguin Dash
entries.summary: Free native Android game. Installed and raced on a Trimui Smart Pro with AndroidRT.
entries.get: Install the author's free Android release directly from this Store entry.
entries.notes: Tested on a Smart Pro: A enters menus, the left stick steers, X jumps, and B backs out cleanly to JukaHub. Sound and other controllers still need testing.

entries.title: Native (NDK) apps and games
entries.summary: Apps and games started from a native arm64 library by NativeActivity or GameActivity are what AndroidRT can try. Penguin Dash has been played on a Smart Pro; other titles need individual testing.
entries.get: Copy APKs you own into the APKs folder on the card, or send them from your phone with the Phone Companion. Your APKs tab checks each one and marks the ones worth trying.
entries.notes: Use the 64-bit (arm64-v8a) build when an app offers one. If it stops, its launch log names what AndroidRT is missing; Java and Kotlin apps still need a full Android runtime.

entries.title: Minecraft: Bedrock Edition
entries.summary: AndroidRT ships a class pack for Minecraft's Java side. Nobody has run it on a handheld yet.
entries.get: Buy Minecraft on Google Play, then copy your own APK off your phone (an APK backup app, or adb). Use the 64-bit (arm64-v8a) build.
entries.notes: The store, the license check and Xbox Live answer as unavailable, never as granted, so a Google Play build may refuse to start without its license. It needs OpenGL ES 3.0 and most of the 1 GB of RAM. Details: docs/ANDROID-MINECRAFT.md.

entries.title: Terraria (mobile edition)
entries.summary: The mobile edition is C#/.NET code running on Mono inside a Java app. AndroidRT runs native (NDK) code only.
entries.route: Terraria's PC version runs on Linux handhelds through FNA with your own game files — the PortMaster route (Start → Games → PortMaster Ports).

entries.title: GameMaker games
entries.summary: GameMaker's Android runner starts in Java, so AndroidRT cannot run these.
entries.route: PortMaster's GMLoader runs a number of GameMaker games from their Android APK on Linux handhelds — look the game up in PortMaster.

entries.title: Unity games
entries.summary: Unity's Android player starts in Java (UnityPlayerActivity) and calls back into it every frame. AndroidRT has no Java runtime, so it cannot run them today.
entries.route: Some Unity games ship a Linux build; PortMaster carries the ones that run on handhelds.

entries.title: Godot, LÖVE and SDL games
entries.summary: Their Android builds start in Java (GodotApp, LÖVE's activity, SDLActivity), which AndroidRT does not provide.
entries.route: These engines all build for Linux: the game's PC version, or its .love file with LÖVE for Linux, usually runs on the handheld through PortMaster.

entries.title: Java and Kotlin apps
entries.summary: Almost every Android app, and most games, is Java/Kotlin bytecode that needs Android's runtime (ART) and framework. AndroidRT is not Android: it loads native game code only.
entries.route: A full Android firmware for the device, or Waydroid on a Linux machine with a binder kernel, runs them. Where Waydroid is set up, the APK Store can install an APK into it.
